newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Greece supports Romania's NATO membership bid.
newsitem.headline: Greece supports Romania's NATO membership bid.

text.p: Visiting Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis on Friday expressed strong support for Romania's bid to join NATO and the European Union, saying it would strengthen cooperation and stability in the Balkans.
"What we (Greece) will do before Madrid is to tell our fellow NATO partners that we support Romania's membership bid," Simitis told a news conference during a two-day visit to the Romanian capital.
Romania is lobbying hard for inclusion in the first wave of North Atlantic Treaty Organisation expansion to be announced at an alliance summit in July.

"It's not certain that Romania won't make the first wave. Nothing is certain yet," Simitis said in reply to a question about the country's chances of being invited in along with more developed east Europeans Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, which are seen as likely first-wave entrants.

His Romanian counterpart, Victor Ciorbea, hailed Simitis' visit, which he said coincided with a U.S.-Russian summit in Helsinki dominated by NATO expansion. Russia has stressed its fierce opposition to bringing in any new members.
"Greece has voiced support for Romania's efforts to join NATO and the EU, whose enlargement should proceed according to clear and non-discriminating criteria," he said.

Greece is the latest NATO member to throw support behind Romania's membership bid, saying it would strengthen the southern flank of the alliance. France, Italy and Turkey have also voiced support for Romanian entry.
Both Ciorbea and Simitis said Bucharest and Athens saw eye to eye on Balkan issues, and called for coordinated efforts to find a peaceful solution to the crisis in Albania.

"We are convinced that Romania's reforms will create the necessary premises in order to attract as many Greek investors as possible," said Ciorbea, whose government has launched tough reforms in a bid to put the economy back on track and attract Western investors.
Ciorbea's centrist coalition government took office after reformists ended the ex-communists' seven-year grip on power in elections last November.
Simitis, accompanied by Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos, is due to meet President Emil Constantinescu later on Friday.
